articles.title: US Open 2026: Gael Monfils wins on 40th birthday to reach New York second round
articles.summary: French veteran Gael Monfils is treated to a rendition of Happy Birthday by the US Open crowd as he becomes the oldest man to win a match there since 1992.
articles.body:
Most people celebrate their 40th birthday with a slap-up meal or a surprise party.

Gael Monfils, the maverick Frenchman who always knows how to have fun on the court, marked his milestone by winning a Grand Slam match at the US Open.

Playing in the final major of his career, Monfils ensured he had a unforgettable night with a 2-6 6-1 6-2 6-0 victory over Paraguayan opponent Adolfo Daniel Vallejo.

The former world number six is the oldest man to win a US Open main-draw match since Jimmy Connors - who also won on his 40th birthday in 1992.

The New York crowd made the occasion even more memorable for Monfils by bursting into an impromptu rendition of Happy Birthday during his post-victory interview.

"To play on my 40th birthday is very special," said the 2016 US Open semi-finalist, who announced last year he will retire at the end of this season.

"The atmosphere [in New York] is always electric - I feel great here. I always try to play great tennis and put on a great show."

Addressing the thousands of fans who created a celebratory atmosphere on Louis Armstrong Stadium, he added: "You guys rock - let's keep it up for the second round."

No repeat of Wimbledon heroics as Fery exits US Open

Gauff's flaw forgotten on winning US Open return

Rybakina makes winning start in race to number one

Playing in his 18th and final US Open, Monfils made a nervous start against 60th-ranked Vallejo.

However, he quickly settled into the match and dominated the next three sets to secure a 131st Grand Slam match win - extending his all-time record for a Frenchman.

It was a typically entertaining display from the charismatic Monfils, who enthralled the crowd with the stylish shot-making and athleticism for which he is known.

"I didn't want to lose first round, that's for sure," said Monfils, who revealed he was given a watch by his wife Elina Svitolina - the two-time Wimbledon semi-finalist - as a birthday present.

"Somehow I felt like even with a sloppy start, I could do better. I kept going for my shots, being versatile with my backhand, tried to use my forehand.

"My rhythm was there and then I had this feeling where I can be in cruise control."

Monfils will continue his farewell appearance at Flushing Meadows against American 14th seed Learner Tien.

Zverev left celebrating at 2am after avoiding shock exit

One man also left celebrating in the early hours of the New York morning was top seed Alexander Zverev.

The 29-year-old German survived a huge scare against Italy's Lorenzo Sonego to win a five-set thriller at almost 2am on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Zverev is aiming to reach the final for the third successive Grand Slam, but almost fell at the first hurdle after being pushed to the limit by 89th-ranked Sonego for almost five hours.

Sonego, 31, produced a stunning performance to lead by two sets to one - and was two points away from victory in the fourth set.

But Zverev, who won the first major of his career at the French Open before reaching the Wimbledon final, showed great resolve to escape with a 6-4 3-6 6-7 (7-9) 7-5 6-4 victory.

"I'm just happy I won - that's it," said Zverev.

"It was an incredible battle with ups and downs. I think it's the longest first round match I've ever played in my life.

"He played amazing tennis and would have beaten a lot of players for sure."

With world number one Jannik Sinner missing through injury, 29-year-old Zverev leads the seedings at a major for the first time in his career.

His prospects also appear to have been aided by Spanish second seed Carlos Alcaraz's lack of match practice following a long-term wrist injury, as well as 24-time major champion Novak Djokovic's own first-round exit on Sunday.

But with that increased sense of opportunity seemed to come more edginess against Sonego.

Zverev, who suffered early exits in Montreal and Cincinnati leading into the US Open, was well below his best again as Sonego threatened to further blow open the men's singles draw.

"This was exactly the sort of match I needed," said Zverev, who goes on to play France's Quentin Halys in the second round.

"I struggled in the last two tournaments, I didn't play well and sometimes good things happen after you fight through one of these matches."

articles.title: US Open: Britain's Arthur Fery admits he still has plenty to work on after his New York debut is cut short
articles.summary: Arthur Fery admits he still has plenty to work on in his game to take on the best players in the world following his first-round exit in New York; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
His hopes of making a splash in New York were ended in the first round after a straight-sets defeat by Lorenzo Musetti .

The 24-year-old had been riding the crest of a wave since his historic run to the Wimbledon semi-finals as a wildcard earlier this summer.

He reached his first ATP final at the Winston-Salem Open last week and arrived at Flushing Meadows with high hopes of another deep run at the Grand Slam.

But he ran aground against Italian 13th seed Musetti in a straight-sets loss on Grandstand Stadium.

It was a comprehensive defeat, but a useful gauge for Fery who has risen from outside the top 200 a year ago to No 33 in the world.

"I know what I have to work on," he said. "I got a lot of ideas coming straight off the court of what I have to work on to do better.

"My serve really let me down today, which is not usually the case, but I've been struggling a little bit to find my rhythm on the serve.

"Today was particularly a struggle, but definitely playing guys at that level, it's tough and the margins are small."

Fery, now the British No 1, was close to being seeded at Flushing Meadows, meaning he would have avoided a player of Musetti's class in the early stages.

He admitted he was under-prepared due to his run in North Carolina last week, but said he would not have done things differently.

"The Grand Slams are the biggest tournaments and everyone has their eye on them." he added. "At the same time, would I sign for these past two weeks? Probably, to be honest.

"It's a lot of ranking points, it's a first ATP final, so it's good. Even though it meant that my preparation for the US Open was not great."

Sky Sports Tennis ' Tim Henman said Fery will take "an enormous amount" from his defeat and will gain vital experience.

The former British No 1 said: "What he lacks right now is experience at the highest level. He's 33 in the world and hasn't played a great deal of tennis outside the UK at this level.

"To come up against Musetti, who is a world-class player, has been five in the world and reached semi-finals of Grand Slams, provides clear evidence of what he needs to work on."

Asked where Fery can improve his game, Henman said: "He's got to continue to give himself opportunities to finish points at the net.

"His forehand side, in these types of [hot] conditions, he can perhaps take the ball a bit earlier and get more penetration through the court.

"He can work on that first serve to get a bit more pace, which is not easy because he's not the tallest of players, but then he's got to improve that accuracy."

Laura Robson said: "Musetti was too good. He had that extra gear to go to with his pace off the racquet and his ability to open up the lines made such a big difference.

"Fery will be a little disappointed that he wasn't able to hang in that first set. That could have changed the course of the match.

"But he came up against such a good opponent."

Broady not expecting Fery to plateau yet

With Fery set to take part in all the big events - including the remaining Masters 1000 events in Shanghai and Paris, former player Naomi Broady expects him to keep improving.

"He's proven himself at the ATP 250 level but now people will start watching him and it becomes a cat and mouse of can he stay ahead of that," said Broady.

"I wouldn't expect him to plateau and the next few months will be exciting. His ranking can still skyrocket."

articles.title: US Open: Top seed Alexander Zverev avoids first-round disaster, holds off Lorenzo Sonego in 5 sets
articles.summary: That could have been a whole lot worse for Alexander Zverev.
articles.body:
That could have been a whole lot worse for Alexander Zverev.

The US Open's top seed avoided a historic first-round upset on Tuesday, holding off Italian challenger Lorenzo Sonego 6-4, 3-6, 6-7 (9-7), 7-5, 6-4 in a late-night, five-hour match at Flushing Meadows. He will face Quentin Halys in the second round.

The time the match ended: 1:55 a.m. local time.

Had Zverev lost, it would have been the sixth time of the Open Era that a No. 1 seed fell in the first round of a major and the first time in more than two decades. The current list: 1971 US Open (John Newcombe), 1990 French Open (Stefan Edberg), 1990 US Open (Edberg), 2002 Australian Open (Lleyton Hewitt) and 2003 Wimbledon (Hewitt).

It was a relatively straightforward first set, with Zverev displaying the form that saw him win Roland-Garros and reach the Wimbledon final this summer. Big first serve. Big second serve. Firm and methodical groundstrokes. It's a hard combination to overcome, and Sonego responded with riskier shots and more trips to the net.

Sonego was redlining: showcasing a higher tolerance for risk against an elite opponent because the usual plan has little hope for success. If it works, you have a match. If it doesn't, you lose by a little more.

For 2 1/2 sets, it worked. Some down-the-line groundstrokes went wide. Some trips to the net resulted in an impossible ball to play. But the winners outpaced the unforced errors for three sets, and it was nearly enough.

There was plenty of nonsense along the way, with Zverev pulled into the kind of match he rarely enjoys.

That aggression saw Sonego only two points from winning the match in four sets, with Zverev serving, but the physical toll of the Italian's all-court play started adding up. Zverev held serve, then immediately broke Sonego to take control of the set and the match.

An early break in the fifth set gave Zverev a comfortable ride to safety.

The numbers from the match won't be encouraging for Zverev, who converted on only 5 of 22 break points and committed nearly as many unforced errors (39) as Sonego (43). That's reason for concern given his early exits at his two previous tournaments in Toronto and Cincinnati.

It was already shaping up to be a chaotic US Open . Jannik Sinner withdrew from the tournament . Novak Djokovic went down in similarly shocking fashion on Sunday . We have no idea if Carlos Alcaraz's wrist and body are ready for a seven-match, five-set tournament after a 4 ½ month layoff.

Outside of Alcaraz and Zverev, the only other player left in the entire field with a Grand Slam singles title to his name is Daniil Medvedev.

It's an environment similar to the one in which Zverev won his Roland-Garros title earlier this year. Once again, he stands to benefit, especially with Alcaraz on the other side of the bracket. If Tuesday is any judge, it won't be as straightforward as it was in Paris.

articles.title: Gauff launches bid for second US Open title with win over Sonmez
articles.summary: Coco Gauff began her bid for a second US Open title with a nerveless win over Zeynep Sonmez. The American fourth seed, champion in 2023, was tested in the se...
articles.body:
Coco Gauff began her bid for a second US Open title with a nerveless win over Zeynep Sonmez.

The American fourth seed, champion in 2023, was tested in the second set by Turkish outsider Sonmez but came through 6-3, 6-4.

She said: "I was nervous in the tunnel, and then for some reason when the warm-up started, it went away. I think it showed the first game how I came out serving really well."

"I don't know what put my mind at ease. I think just maybe the confidence I had this week and knowing, like, you know, the opponent would have to play a really high level and me a really low level, maybe for it to not go my way."

"But Zeynep brought that high level today. Yeah, I was just happy to get out of that second set."

Second seed Elena Rybakina also advanced after beating teenage US wild card Thea Frodin 6-3, 6-2.

Frodin once played Serena Williams' double in the tennis scenes during the Oscar-winning film about the lives of Serena and her sister Venus, King Richard, starring Will Smith.

She said: "I actually have not met her yet. But hopefully I can get the chance soon to get the opportunity to meet her."

"I saw that Will Smith reposted one of my posts, so that was pretty cool and a cool experience."

Switzerland's Belinda Bencic was fortunate to avoid being defaulted after whacking a ball into the crowd.

The 29-year-old, seeded 12th, swatted a ball in frustration after losing a point, and then turned in horror after realizing where it had flown.

She raised her arms in apology and was given a warning by the umpire, but opponent Yulia Putintseva clearly felt the punishment should have been harsher.

However, Kazakhstani Putintseva eventually won the match over three sets to send Bencic packing anyway.

In the men's draw, fifth seed Flavio Cobolli needed five sets to see off Argentinian Francisco Comesana, while ninth seed Taylor Fritz - one of the big hopes for a home success in New York this year - beat fellow American Darwin Blanch in three.

Frenchman Gael Monfils, who retires at the end of the year, celebrated his 40th birthday in style with a 2-6, 6-2, 6-1, 6-0 victory over Adolfo Alvarez.

A late-night marathon on Arthur Ashe Stadium saw Alexander Zverev narrowly avoid becoming only the fourth top-seeded man to lose in the first round of a grand slam in the open era.

The German, who won the French Open and reached the Wimbledon final this year, trailed Italian Lorenzo Sonego by two sets to one.

But Zverev clawed his way back and eventually won in five, 6-4, 3-6, 6-7 (7-9), 7-5, 6-4.

The four-hour-and-53-minute slog finished at 1:55 am local time.

articles.title: Zverev wins wild five-setter, Rybakina and Gauff ease through at US Open

articles.body:
Top-seeded Alexander Zverev survived a scare, overcoming Lorenzo Sonego in a wild-five setter at the US Open on Tuesday as Elena Rybakina and Coco Gauff advanced with ease.

Zverev fought off a determined challenge from Italy's lowly ranked Sonego, winning 6-4, 3-6, 6-7 (7/9), 7-5, 6-4.

Zverev fought off a determined challenge from Sonego in a tense all-court battle spiced by unlikely retrievals, impossibly angled winners and some inexplicable errors, which wrapped up on Arthur Ashe Stadium after four hours and 53 minutes at 1:55 in the morning.

"I'm just happy I won, that's it. Incredible battle," said Zverev, who was two points from defeat trailing 5-4 in the fourth set.

The German held serve and broke Sonego in the next game, then earned the lone break of the fifth set to complete the win.

Zverev, who followed his first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros with a Wimbledon final appearance, notched his seventh win in as many matches against Sonego, ranked 89 in the world.

"Credit to him, he played an incredible match," Zverev said, adding it was just the kind of battle he needed after lackluster performances in two hard court tournaments coming into the Open.

There was no such drama for world number two Rybakina and former champion Gauff.

Rybakina, eyeing a third Grand Slam title and the world number one ranking, beat US teen Thea Frodin 6-3, 6-2.

Gauff showed off her immensely improved serve in a confident 6-3, 6-4 victory over 53rd-ranked Zeynep Sonmez of Turkey.

Gauff blazed through the opening set before Sonmez upped her game, recovering an early break in the second and briefly taking the lead before Gauff regrouped.

"I think I was just trying not to panic," Gauff said. "She started coming to the net and playing great tennis.

"That 3-all game was real important," added Gauff, who saved three break points in the sixth game and broke in the next for a lead she wouldn't relinquish.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina showed little sign of the left heel injury that forced her out of her quarter-final in Cincinnati this month.

She saved both break points she faced in a polished performance against the big-hitting if erratic American, who was playing her first Grand Slam main draw match on a wild card.

"I'm happy with the match. Especially when you don't know your opponent, it always can be dangerous, but overall I'm happy with the first match and how it went," she said.

Women's French Open champion Mirra Andreeva also advanced easily, cruising past Indonesia's 36th-ranked Janice Tjen 6-2, 6-2.

Andreeva, seeded fifth, has had a lackluster run on North American hard courts since her scintillating run to a first Grand Slam title in Paris.

But she was dialed in as she produced her second win over Tien in less than two weeks.

After a tough win against the Indonesian in Cincinnati, Andreeva said, "I was just trying to be very aggressive."

Fifth-seeded Flavio Cobolli, runner-up to Zverev at Roland Garros, rallied from two sets down for the first time in his career to beat Argentina's Francisco Comesana 3-6, 2-6, 6-3, 6-4, 6-4.

The Italian shook off an erratic start, dropping to his knees and raising his arms in celebration after closing out the four-hour, 13-minute marathon.

"In a Grand Slam it's never done," Cobolli said. "You have to fight to the last point."

In the time it took Cobolli and Comesana to battle it out on the Louis Armstrong stadium, Americans Madison Keys and Taylor Fritz both posted wins on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Keys, a former Australian Open winner who lost in the first round at Flushing Meadows last year, conquered first-match jitters to beat 19-year-old Russian Alina Korneeva 7-5, 6-4.

Nerves didn't seem to be a problem for ninth-seeded Fritz as he sailed past fellow American Darwin Blanch 6-3, 6-2, 6-4.

While play went as scheduled on the covered Ashe and Armstrong stadiums, those on outside courts -- including Rybakina -- had to wait out some lengthy rain delays.

That included a near four-hour delay to the start of play and more delays in the evening. Five late matches were postponed altogether and a handful of others suspended to resume on Wednesday.
